explorations.title: Mushrooms
explorations.summary: A forest-floor investigation of fungi, mushroom structures, spores, and the hidden work of decomposers.

image.alt: Mushrooms growing together on a forest floor.

learningPoints: Fungi are different from plants and animals
Mushrooms help return nutrients to an ecosystem
Careful observation reveals many shapes, textures, and structures

explorations.title: Butterflies in the Classroom
explorations.summary: Follow a remarkable classroom life cycle from tiny caterpillars through chrysalis changes to newly emerged butterflies.

image.alt: A caterpillar representing the classroom butterfly life-cycle exploration.

learningPoints: A butterfly changes through four distinct life-cycle stages
Growth can be documented with dates, drawings, and measurements
Living classroom guests require gentle, responsible care

explorations.title: Great Barrier Reef
explorations.summary: Dive into coral reef habitats, meet the animals that depend on them, and investigate why healthy oceans matter.

image.alt: Sea turtle illustration from the Great Barrier Reef exploration.

learningPoints: Coral reefs are living habitats built by tiny animals
Reef species depend on one another in a connected ecosystem
People can make choices that help protect ocean habitats

twwl.title: Botany: Let’s Talk About Tubers
twwl.summary: We dug into botany to discover how tubers store energy, grow underground, and help plants begin again.

image.alt: Botany illustration used for the Tubers learning story.

image.alt: Winter illustration used for the Russian Winter learning story.

twwl.title: Silent Wings, Wise Eyes: Learning About Owls
twwl.summary: We investigated owl adaptations and learned what makes these birds such skilled nighttime hunters.

image.alt: Owl illustration used for the owl learning story.

twwl.title: Bats Don’t Go Bump in the Night
twwl.summary: We explored echolocation, nocturnal adaptations, and the many ways bats help their ecosystems.

twwl.title: Autumn Spiders: Gentle Web Artists
twwl.summary: We studied silk, web patterns, body structures, and the helpful role spiders play in an ecosystem.
